q: Why were early predictions about public libraries gloomy?
options: Fewer people were able to read printed books.
Experts thought that digital reading would make library buildings unnecessary.
Libraries were too expensive to build.
Most librarians wanted to retire.
explain: Eksperci pytali, kto będzie potrzebował budynku pełnego papieru, skoro książki można kupić online.

q: According to the text, why do more people visit libraries today?
options: Libraries sell books at lower prices.
Libraries have become much bigger.
More people have stopped using the Internet.
Libraries now work as meeting places with many activities.
explain: Biblioteki "have become meeting places" i oferują znacznie więcej niż regały.

q: What does the text say about language cafés?
options: They teach foreign languages to local children.
Newcomers practise the local language there with volunteers.
They are open only to university students.
They replace regular language courses.
explain: Przybysze ćwiczą język z wolontariuszami przy herbacie.

q: Why may a library be especially important for some people?
options: It lends them money for their studies.
It offers free medical advice.
It finds them a job directly.
It gives them access to a computer to apply for jobs and fill in forms.
explain: Bez komputera w domu biblioteka bywa jedynym miejscem do składania podań i formularzy online.

q: What do critics of modern libraries claim?
options: Libraries should be closed completely.
Libraries should sell e-books.
A library with too few books is no longer a real library.
Librarians are not well educated.
explain: Krytycy twierdzą, że biblioteka bez wystarczającej liczby książek przestaje być biblioteką.

q: How do librarians answer the critics?
options: They say that collections now include digital materials.
They agree and plan to buy more shelves.
They ask the government for more volunteers.
They refuse to comment.
explain: Zbiory się rozrosły o e-booki, audiobooki i cyfrowe czasopisma.

q: What did the director of the northern library consider the key to success?
options: Opening on Sundays only.
Hiring more librarians.
Asking residents about their needs before planning.
Copying a famous library abroad.
explain: Dyrektorka mówi, że klucz to pytanie mieszkańców, czego potrzebują, i słuchanie ich.

q: What is the author's final message?
options: A library's value lies in the people it serves, not in the number of books.
Libraries will disappear within a few years.
Only large libraries can survive.
Books are no longer important.
explain: Autor kończy myślą, że wartość biblioteki mierzy się liczbą ludzi, nie liczbą książek.

q: Which paragraph explains why the five-day week was introduced in the first place?
explain: Akapit 1: pięciodniowy tydzień upowszechnił się, bo zmęczeni pracownicy popełniali więcej błędów.

q: Which paragraph describes a trial in which employees did not lose any salary?
explain: Akapit 2: pracownicy zachowali pełne pensje, choć pracowali 32 godziny zamiast 40.

q: Which paragraph mentions improvements in the private lives of employees?
explain: Akapit 3: więcej snu, czasu z rodziną i na hobby.

q: Which paragraph suggests that the results of the trials may not be typical?
explain: Akapit 4: ekonomiści zauważają, że próby były małe, a firmy zgłosiły się same.

q: Which paragraph discusses jobs that cannot simply stop work on certain days?
explain: Akapit 5: szpital nie może być zamknięty w piątek, a sklep otwarty siedem dni potrzebuje obsady.

q: Which paragraph mentions a change in the way employers judge success?
explain: Akapit 6: pracodawcy zaczęli oceniać wyniki, a nie liczbę godzin w biurze.

q: Which paragraph reports that fewer employees left their jobs?
explain: Akapit 2: kilka firm odnotowało mniejszą liczbę odejść z pracy.

q: Which paragraph gives the opinion of economists?
explain: Akapit 4 zaczyna się od zastrzeżeń ekonomistów.

q: Which paragraph mentions that sick leave decreased?
explain: Akapit 3: menedżerowie zauważyli mniej zwolnień chorobowych.

q: What did many residents expect when the Wi-Fi switch-off was announced?
options: A celebration.
A fall in tourism.
Protests.
A new council.
explain: Mieszkańcy spodziewali się protestów, ale reakcja była inna.

q: What happened in the village square after the first week?
options: It filled with people who talked to each other.
It was closed to the public.
It became a car park.
It was used only by teenagers.
explain: Plac się zapełnił, a ludzie siedzieli przy tych samych stolikach.

q: Who proposed the experiment?
options: A café owner.
A university researcher.
A teacher worried about teenagers' breaks.
A group of parents.
explain: Pomysł miała nauczycielka, która zauważyła nastolatków wpatrzonych w ekrany.

q: On what condition did the council agree to the experiment?
options: The shops would remain connected to the internet.
The experiment would last three months.
The university would pay for it.
Teenagers would not take part.
explain: Sklepy miały zachować internet, żeby nikt nie był odcięty od niezbędnych usług.

q: How did some young people react?
options: They moved to a neighbouring town.
They organised a football match.
They thanked the council.
They complained of being treated like children and met outside the village.
explain: Część młodych narzekała i spotykała się na parkingu poza wsią, gdzie był zasięg.

q: Why do the researchers advise caution about the results?
options: The experiment was not finished.
One month is short and August is a holiday period.
Only adults took part.
Nobody collected any data.
explain: Według badaczy miesiąc to za mało, a sierpień to czas wakacji.

q: What does the village plan for the next summer?
options: To close all the shops.
To build a new Wi-Fi network.
To end the experiment.
To repeat the project with more events in the square.
explain: Wieś chce powtórzyć projekt z dłuższym programem wydarzeń na placu.

q: Which paragraph discusses the environmental cost of demolishing buildings?
explain: Akapit 3: demolka produkuje odpady, a energia włożona w budowę przepada ("embodied energy").

q: Which paragraph mentions income from tourism?
explain: Akapit 2: zabytkowe dzielnice przynoszą pieniądze od turystów.

q: Which paragraph describes difficulties such as heating and access for disabled people?
explain: Akapit 5: stare domy są zimne i trudne do dostosowania dla osób z niepełnosprawnościami.

q: Which paragraph suggests that old buildings help people feel connected to a place?
explain: Akapit 4: znajome ulice i domy dają mieszkańcom poczucie związku z okolicą.

q: Which paragraph gives examples of buildings that were given a new function?
explain: Akapit 6: dworce w muzea, fabryki w mieszkania, hala targowa w bibliotekę.

q: Which paragraph mentions the problem of waste?
explain: Akapit 3 mówi o dużych ilościach odpadów z rozbiórki.

q: Which paragraph states that renovation can be cheaper than new construction?
explain: Akapit 2: remont starego budynku bywa tańszy niż budowa nowego.

q: Which paragraph says that many cities prefer modern buildings?
explain: Akapit 1: władze wielu miast wolą nowoczesną zabudowę.
